description: Fixed VS-SP-001 root-cause benchmark for the M4 exit gate (section 26.1): the Rs bias-insensitive anomaly on a PN phase shifter, diagnosed from a normalized mock device project. NOT CHERRY-PICKED: the mechanism catalog was written first, then one case per mechanism and per operating condition the loop must survive (a recurrence, a licence outage, a closed lab, a non-converged solver), each with its expected stop written before any loop was run. Cases the loop cannot resolve are included and expected to end unresolved. Devices are mock projects: the fault is visible only as the geometry or configuration that would cause it, never as a label the backends read. VERSION 1.1.0 (candidate, for the owner's decision): the expectations under the candidate declarations sp.rs_anomaly_mechanisms@1.1.0, which leave three links to a person because their check cannot observe what the link claims (Causal Warrant Gate V1.1, review 04). Two 1.0.0 cases change their expected stop; each states the 1.0.0 expectation and why. Three regression cases from review 04 are added. UNLIKE 1.0.0, these expectations were NOT all written before any loop ran: an experiment on 2026-10-15 had already run the two changed cases under the same withdrawals. Cases marked known_limitation state the scientifically correct outcome that neither declaration version reaches. REVISED after an independent science review of the candidate, 2026-10-20 (94 episodes under both declaration versions): probe-lab-closed keeps 1.0.0's expected stop, now for the stated reason, and is a known limitation of 1.1.0; the truth of the two mesh cases is corrected; five of the review's counterexamples are added, each a known limitation.
question: Why is Rs extremely high and weakly bias dependent while Cj trends normally
symptom: Rs extremely high and weakly bias-dependent while Cj trends normally
expected_behavior: Rs per length of the design order, falling slightly with reverse bias as the access region depletes
observed_behavior: Rs per length several times the design value, flat across the reverse-bias sweep; Cj falls with reverse bias as designed

evidence.text: rs extremely high and weakly bias dependent while cj trends normally on the phase shifter
an earlier charge simulation of this device reported a convergence warning in the access region
high series resistance with flat bias often comes from a contact via or access region defect
review of series resistance extraction and normalization in carrier depletion phase shifters
counterdoping in the rib raises the series resistance of pn phase shifters
probe contact resistance inflates series resistance in two point measurements

contact_discontinuity.statement: An access or contact discontinuity dominates the series resistance.
assumptions: the contact via geometry is taken unmodified from the device project
contact_discontinuity.falsifier: the connectivity inspection finds every contact tied to metal with full overlap

normalization_error.statement: A length normalization error in extraction inflates the per-length resistance.
assumptions: the extraction divides by a single device length
confounders: taper sections excluded from the drawn length
normalization_error.falsifier: the extraction's normalization length matches the drawn length

mesh_artifact.statement: A mesh convergence artifact in the access region inflates the extracted series resistance.
assumptions: the solver mesh in the access region is the project default
mesh_artifact.falsifier: refining the access mesh leaves the extracted Rs unchanged

dopant_compensation.statement: Counter-doping compensates the rib and raises the resistance of the undepleted access path.
assumptions: the implant recipe matches the process design kit
dopant_compensation.falsifier: the DC sweep shows the design free-carrier density in the access region

probe_artifact.statement: Probe contact resistance in the two-point measurement inflates the reported series resistance.
assumptions: the anomaly was measured with a two point probe
probe_artifact.falsifier: a four point measurement reports the same series resistance

cases.note: cathode via never drawn to metal
a recurrence on another device: anode via overlap below the rule; the earlier case is on record
extraction divides by the taper-inclusive 1000 um instead of the drawn 500 um
access-region mesh edge 40 nm, well above the resolution length
cases.truth: not a mesh artifact: the device is physically nominal and only its simulation mesh is coarse, which can inflate a SIMULATED resistance but not the MEASURED one; the cause of the measured anomaly is not in this case
cases.rationale: 1.1.0 leaves the mesh class's signature (UNSTABLE) to a person: a coarse access mesh makes a simulated resistance unreliable, but the observed anomaly is a measured one and the declaration cannot tell the two apart. Nothing else the cheap checks observe settles the rivals, so the loop stops at the next discriminating action, the four-point probe, which needs a person. The 1.0.0 confirmation of a mesh artifact as the cause of a measured anomaly was the category error review 04 named. Even after the probe, this episode cannot conclude today: an observed UNSTABLE still counts as the mesh class's declared signature and holds back every other class's confirmation (independent science review of the candidate, 2026-10-20).

cases.note: the only simulator seat is held by another job; the fault is a contact the inspection can see
the only simulator seat is held by another job; the fault needs a solve
cases.truth: not a mesh artifact: the device is physically nominal and only its simulation mesh is coarse, which can inflate a SIMULATED resistance but not the MEASURED one; the cause of the measured anomaly is not in this case

cases.note: the design is sound; the anomaly is the two-point measurement
the design is sound and the probe station is unavailable: nothing sufficient remains
cases.rationale: The probe artifact -- this case's truth -- is tested only by the four-point probe, and the probe station is closed: the right stop names what is left open and waits for it. No sufficient action remains: the split lot produces only a carrier profile, so it cannot discriminate the contact class, does not test the probe artifact, and is an irreversible fabrication of new devices. 1.0.0 reaches this stop, but by refuting the contact and dopant classes on design-file readings that cannot see fabricated faults.
cases.known_limitation: 1.1.0 no longer refutes contact and dopant on design-file readings, and then asks for a split lot (6 weeks, $40k, irreversible) that cannot settle the question: an unjustified escalation. A closed station should be a temporary resource, and an irreversible fabrication should not be the next step while a rival's declared check is only temporarily unavailable (independent science review of the candidate, 2026-10-20).

cases.note: counter-doped, but the solver does not converge: coarse evidence may challenge and may not confirm (SIM-002)
review 04 V2: two faults, an open cathode via and a taper-inclusive 1000 um normalization; each has a cheap check
cases.rationale: Both cheap checks run and each observes its class's signature. Two classes are supported, so the loop names both and confirms neither.

cases.note: review 04 V3: the anomaly is the two-point measurement; the extraction's length is 510 um against 500 um drawn
cases.rationale: A 2 % length mismatch cannot account for a resistance several times the design value, so the normalization class must not be confirmed; the four-point probe is the discriminating action.
cases.known_limitation: the normalization signature (DISAGREES, more than 1 % mismatch) is blind to size; 1.0.0 and 1.1.0 both confirm a normalization error here. A size-aware signature is the domain expert's decision.

cases.note: review 04 V4: the anomaly is the two-point measurement; the extraction's length is 250 um against 500 um drawn
cases.rationale: The pack's extraction scales the resistance by the normalization length (R x L), so a SHORTER length lowers the reported per-length value: it cannot explain an inflated one. The normalization class must not be confirmed.
cases.known_limitation: the normalization signature is blind to direction; 1.0.0 and 1.1.0 both confirm a normalization error here. A directional signature is the domain expert's decision.

cases.note: review counterexample C1: counter-doping 3E17 against the 5E17 rib, and a coarse 40 nm access mesh in the simulation
cases.rationale: The rib is counter-doped; the coarse mesh affects only the simulation and cannot explain a measured anomaly. Dopant compensation is the cause.
cases.known_limitation: 1.0.0 confirms the mesh artifact; 1.1.0 supports dopant compensation but the observed UNSTABLE, still the mesh class's declared signature, holds the confirmation back, and no answer releases it.
cases.source: independent science review of the candidate, 2026-10-20

cases.note: review counterexample C13: as dopant-with-coarse-mesh, with the probe station closed
cases.rationale: As dopant-with-coarse-mesh; the closed probe station changes nothing about the cause.
cases.known_limitation: 1.0.0 confirms the mesh artifact; 1.1.0 stops awaiting a review whose answer, either way, cannot confirm dopant compensation.
cases.source: independent science review of the candidate, 2026-10-20

cases.note: review counterexample C2: anode via overlap 95 nm against a 100 nm rule
cases.rationale: A 95 nm overlap against a 100 nm rule adds at most a few percent of contact resistance, not a several-fold Rs: the rule flag must not confirm a contact discontinuity. The four-point probe is the discriminating action.
cases.known_limitation: the contact signature (any rule violation is DISCONTINUOUS) is blind to size; both versions confirm a contact discontinuity.
cases.source: independent science review of the candidate, 2026-10-20

cases.note: review counterexample C10: counter-doping 3E17 and an anode overlap of 95 nm
cases.rationale: The 95 nm overlap cannot explain a several-fold Rs; the counter-doped rib can. The DC sweep that observes it must run before anything is confirmed.
cases.known_limitation: both versions confirm a contact discontinuity on the size-blind signature, and the dopant check never runs.
cases.source: independent science review of the candidate, 2026-10-20

cases.note: review counterexample C3: counter-doping 1.6E17 against the 5E17 rib (ratio 0.32)
cases.rationale: A compensation ratio of 0.32 raises the access resistivity about 1.5 to 1.7 times, not several-fold: it is present, but it does not account for the anomaly.
cases.known_limitation: the dopant signature (ratio above 0.3 is COMPENSATED) over-claims magnitude; both versions confirm dopant compensation.
cases.source: independent science review of the candidate, 2026-10-20
